note: Narrow-spectrum oral tetracycline (sarecycline/Seysara, approved 2018) for moderate-to-severe acne; the DB class was unresolved (ChEMBL mechanism 'Unknown'), so the class is defined here by hand with minocycline/doxycycline as broader-class comparators.
label: Acne (sarecycline)

engagement.note: Sarecycline MIC50 0.5 µg/mL against 55 C. acnes isolates, equal to other tetracyclines; no patient C. acnes or skin-microbiome measurement has been published.
engagement.short: C. acnes MIC equals older tetracyclines
engagement.quote: The MIC values for sarecycline ranged from 0.5 to 16 µg/ml; the MIC50 was 0.5 µg/ml, and the MIC90 was 4 µg/ml.
engagement.reason: No patient C. acnes measurement published
engagement.judgement: Target = C. acnes (plus anti-inflammatory action). No published sarecycline study measures C. acnes burden or skin microbiome in patients; the only human microbiome comparison (NCT07544251, sarecycline vs doxycycline, gut + skin) is recruiting (start 2026-04-20). The 2018 label states 'The mechanism of action of SEYSARA in treating acne vulgaris is not known' (12.1) and carries no Microbiology section. Ribosome structures (Batool 2020 PNAS; Lomakin 2023 NAR, C. acnes 70S) are target-engagement models with no patient read-out.

efficacy.note: Phase 2 paper states the design rationale: narrow in-vitro spectrum; no accepted animal model of acne exists, so efficacy rested on MICs.
efficacy.short: No acne animal model; MICs only
efficacy.quote: Sarecycline is a novel, tetracycline-class antibiotic specifically designed for acne, offering a narrow spectrum of activity compared with currently available tetracyclines, including less activity against enteric Gram-negative bacteria.
efficacy.judgement: Opener only. J Drugs Dermatol 2018;17(3):333-338 carries no DOI (PubMed URL used); abstract-level. Earliest citable statement that the in-vitro spectrum model existed for this class; the Phase 2 trial itself ran in 2012 (NCT01628549), so the model is older than 2018 but no earlier citable source was found. Bunick 2021 (doi 10.3390/antibiotics10040439) states 'Since no accepted animal model of acne has been developed to date, the efficacy of sarecycline in vivo was assessed using infection models in CD-1 mice'.

efficacy.note: In-vitro C. acnes activity equal to older tetracyclines; both Phase 3 trials met IGA and lesion endpoints (IGA success 21.9%/22.6% vs 10.5%/15.3%).
efficacy.short: Phase 3 met endpoints as MICs implied
efficacy.quote: These findings support sarecycline as a narrow-spectrum tetracycline-class antibiotic that is effective for the treatment of acne, and further investigation into the potential reduced effects on the gut microbiome compared with those of other agents is warranted.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call. Zhanel 2019 (Allergan authors; full text read, open access) reports C. acnes MICs equal to minocycline/doxycycline, cites in its introduction that both Phase 3 trials 'met the 12-week primary efficacy endpoint', and concludes the in-vitro findings support an effective acne antibiotic. That is a juxtaposition, not a quantitative prediction: no source links MIC or anti-inflammatory potency to the effect size, and the FDA label says mechanism (12.1) and pharmacodynamics (12.2) in acne are unknown. Bunick 2021 (PubMed-typed Review, but first report of the rat carrageenan paw-edema data, on file with Almirall) repeats the juxtaposition: 'Sarecycline has also demonstrated efficacy in reducing inflammatory acne lesions in pivotal clinical trials'. Patient numbers from the FDA label Table 2 (Study 1 NCT02320149 n=968; Study 2 NCT02322866 n=1034). Downgrade to untested if juxtaposition without a stated prediction is ruled insufficient.

safety.model: In-vitro gut-flora MIC panel + mouse E. coli septicemia
safety.note: Narrow spectrum (16–32× less active on enteric Gram-negatives) predicted less gut dysbiosis and fewer GI/candidal adverse events than minocycline/doxycycline.
safety.short: Gut-sparing spectrum predicts fewer GI AEs
safety.quote: It offers a narrow antibacterial spectrum relative to other tetracycline options, which may lead to less selective pressure on enteric Gram-negative bacteria, resulting in less disruption of commensal organisms and less potential for antibiotic resistance.
safety.judgement: Opener only; same source caveats as the efficacy opener (no DOI, abstract-level). The 16-32x figure and the mouse E. coli septicemia PD50 (>40 vs 5.72 mg/kg doxycycline) are from Zhanel 2019.

safety.model: In-vitro gut-flora MIC panel + mouse E. coli septicemia
safety.note: Phase 3 GI adverse events low, diarrhoea equal to placebo, candidiasis rare; but no active comparator and no human microbiome study, which the authors request.
safety.short: GI AEs low, as spectrum predicted
safety.quote: The rates of adverse events associated with the gastrointestinal tract, such as nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, were generally low, while the rate of diarrhea in patients treated with sarecycline was comparable to that in patients treated with placebo.
safety.reason: Low GI AEs; no comparator arm
safety.judgement: Zhanel 2019 Discussion states the prediction ('may result in reduced dysbiosis of the intestinal flora ... reduced gastrointestinal adverse effects, such as diarrhea') and then reports the Phase 3 GI/candidiasis rates (label: nausea 3.1% vs 2.0% placebo; vulvovaginal candidiasis 0.6%). The match is implicit and direction-only: the trials were placebo-controlled with no minocycline/doxycycline arm, and the authors themselves call for in-vitro gut models or studies 'in acne patients or healthy volunteers'. Later work: Ghannoum 2022 (doi 10.3390/antibiotics11030324) and Moura 2022 (doi 10.3389/fmicb.2022.901911) are in-vitro gut models, not patients; the first human microbiome RCT (NCT07544251) is recruiting (2026). Vestibular: Grada 2022 (doi 10.3389/fmed.2022.1033980; rat IV dosing, sarecycline undetectable in brain vs minocycline) states 'may explain low rates of vestibular-related adverse events seen in clinical trials' — a primary non-clinical-vs-clinical comparison, but run after the trials (retrodiction), status unchanged so no extra entry. Phototoxicity: Phase 3 vestibular and phototoxic TEAEs each <=1% (Moore 2018, J Drugs Dermatol 17:987, no DOI); Pariser 2019 reports a Phase 1 human phototoxicity study (J Clin Aesthet Dermatol 12(11):E53, no DOI; full text not in PMC) with no preclinical phototoxicity model comparison found. General toxicology models in the label (13.1): 2-year mouse and rat carcinogenicity, rat fertility, rat micronucleus; the FDA review exists as a single multi-discipline review (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/209521Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf, >10 MB) but could not be read this session (fetch size cap; direct download blocked), so model_filed is null for every entry — the label alone does not name the MIC or mouse models. Label 5.3/5.5 word CNS and photosensitivity warnings as tetracycline-class effects.
